Contingency for third-party services (email, search, tracing)

assumptions: The rate card provided is a PLACEHOLDER: all team members are listed generically as 'Team member' at $75/hour with only 1 FTE available. Costs below are indicative only until real roles (e.g. backend, frontend, QA, DevOps) and their respective hourly rates are assigned.

With only 1 FTE available across the whole project, the backlog (24 tasks, ~168 story points) must be delivered sequentially by a single person. This is a major capacity constraint: at a rough conversion of 1 point ≈ 8-10 hours (including design, build, test, review), total effort is estimated at ~2,226 hours, which equates to over a year of full-time work (2,226 hrs / ~1,880 hrs per FTE-year ≈ 1.2 years) for one person alone, before accounting for illness, leave, or context-switching overhead.

No historical actuals (real spend/velocity data) exist for this project yet, so hours-per-point conversions are estimated using generic industry rule-of-thumb ratios rather than observed team velocity. This is a significant source of estimating risk.

Story points were converted to hours at approximately 10 hours/point for high-complexity/high-risk items (integrations, migrations, security) and 8 hours/point for more standard CRUD/UI items, then summed across all 24 backlog items.

Non-labour costs are rough placeholders for third-party tooling/services (CI infrastructure, Stripe fees/tooling, Oracle migration tooling, misc. SaaS for email/search/tracing) since no vendor quotes were supplied.

Scenario spread (Low/Most likely/High) reflects uncertainty inherent in single-resource delivery, unclear legacy data quality (PW-8), and integration risk (PW-7 Stripe, PW-8 Oracle migration) rather than differences in scope.
Priority breakdown allocates each task's estimated labour cost to its stated priority bucket (Urgent, High, Medium, Low) to show where budget concentration lies.

It is assumed the client wants a single blended estimate across the full backlog rather than a phased/sprint-by-sprint budget; re-estimation is strongly recommended once real roles and rates are defined and once actual velocity data exists.
input.reasoning: Since the rate card only provides one generic 'Team member' role at $75/hr with 1 FTE, I could not break the estimate down by specialized roles (backend, frontend, QA, DevOps, etc.) as would normally be done for a project of this shape. Instead, I converted the 24 backlog items' story points into estimated hours using standard point-to-hour heuristics (8-10 hrs/point depending on complexity/risk), reflecting that items like Legacy Data Migration (PW-8, 21 pts), Payment Provider Integration (PW-7, 13 pts), RBAC (PW-4, 13 pts) and Multi-currency (PW-14, 13 pts) carry higher integration/data risk and were weighted at the higher end. This produced a total of ~2,226 hours at $75/hr = $166,950 in labour cost. I added non-labour line items for third-party tooling/services implicated by specific backlog items (CI/staging infra for PW-1, Stripe tooling for PW-7, Oracle migration tooling for PW-8, and a general contingency for smaller SaaS dependencies like email/search/tracing used in PW-11/PW-13/PW-22), totalling $6,500. This gives a most-likely total of $173,450. I derived optimistic (-15%) and pessimistic (+25%) scenarios to reflect the substantial uncertainty from: (a) a placeholder rate card with only 1 FTE trying to absorb a ~168-point backlog, (b) unknown legacy data quality for the Oracle migration, and (c) no historical velocity data to validate the point-to-hour conversion. I flagged the single-FTE capacity constraint explicitly as this is likely the single biggest risk to schedule and cost — the backlog as scoped cannot realistically be delivered by 1 FTE in a normal project timeframe, and either headcount must increase or scope/timeline must be renegotiated.

reductions.description: Descope Legacy Admin Back-office (PW-18, Low priority, 13 pts) from this phase — defer to a later release since it serves internal support staff, not customers.
reductions.effect: Removes ~130 hours of build/test effort; internal support agents continue using existing manual processes until a later phase.

reductions.description: Defer Usage Analytics and Reporting (PW-19, Low priority, 8 pts) and Contract Tests against Helpdesk API (PW-23, Low priority, 5 pts) to a post-launch phase.
reductions.effect: Removes ~104 hours; finance dashboards and contract-test safety net are delivered later once core portal is live, accepting some short-term integration risk with the helpdesk.

reductions.description: Drop Support Ticket Submission (PW-12, Low priority, 5 pts) from this phase and have customers continue using existing helpdesk channels directly.
reductions.effect: Removes ~50 hours; no in-portal ticket submission at launch, slightly less convenient customer support workflow initially.

reductions.description: Simplify Multi-currency support (PW-14, 13 pts) to launch with a single currency (USD) and add EUR/PLN in a later iteration.
reductions.effect: Removes ~78 hours; reduces FX-rate integration and settlement complexity for MVP launch at the cost of limiting initial addressable market to USD customers.

reductions.description: Increase headcount beyond the current 1 FTE placeholder, or explicitly extend timeline, rather than trying to compress ~2,226 hours of work into a single resource.
reductions.effect: No direct dollar saving, but prevents hidden cost/schedule overruns from context-switching fatigue, single-point-of-failure risk, and unrealistic delivery timelines that a 1-FTE plan would otherwise incur.
